subject: Medicore RFP — Safeguard clauses & Order Form exposure matrix
messages:
From: Jared Simmons <j.simmons@medicore.com>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@medicore.com, legal@medicore.com
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: RFP legal follow-up — liability caps & order form schedule

Chloe — thanks for the demo last week. Attached is the set of legal questions our counsel has consolidated after reviewing the draft order form and exhibits. High level asks: clarify IP ownership for model outputs, proposed liability cap tiers, and whether Redwood will accept a carve-out for IP indemnity limited to third-party claims only.

Two time-sensitive items:
- We need an updated Order Form (pricing + SLA table) with the liabilities matrix by Wednesday 2026-08-21 for our procurement committee.
- Our counsel prefers a 2x fees liability cap for service-level financial exposure and a carve-out for willful misconduct. Can Redwood confirm approach?

Appreciate a concise redline or a response matrix.

Thanks,
Jared Simmons
Sr. Procurement Manager
Medicore Health Systems
procurement@medicore.com

Attachment: Medicore_RFP_Legal_Questions.pdf (pdf, 145KB)

From: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>
To: Jared Simmons <j.simmons@medicore.com>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com, evelyn.hart@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: RFP legal follow-up — liability caps & order form schedule

Jared — thanks for the note and the doc. Looping Laura (legal ops) and Evelyn (sales lead) so we can turn around a clear matrix. Quick confirmations up front:

- IP / outputs: Redwood does not claim customers' output. We grant customers a perpetual, worldwide right to use outputs generated by their prompts; we propose a mutual covenant that neither party will claim ownership over the other party's pre-existing IP.

- Liability cap: Our standard is a fee-based cap; we typically propose 3x the annualized fees for the 12-month term or a fixed $5M cap for enterprise. We're open to a 2x cap conversation if there are reciprocal protections and a clear carve-out structure for IP claims.

- IP indemnity: Redwood can indemnify customers for third-party IP infringement claims arising from our model weights or tooling, subject to notice and cooperation requirements, and typical indemnity ceilings. Redwood cannot accept uncapped attorney fee obligations or unlimited consequential damages.

Planned deliverable: a redlined Order Form + a short response matrix addressing each of Medicore's bullets by EOD 2026-08-20. If procurement needs the table earlier, we can provide a summary matrix by 2026-08-19.

Proposed next step: 30-min legal sync on Thursday 2026-08-20 10:00 AM PT to walk authors through carve-outs and the SLA schedule. Does that work?

Best,
Chloe Martin
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
chloe.martin@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0182

From: laura.bennett@redwood.com <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>, Jared Simmons <j.simmons@medicore.com>
Cc: evelyn.hart@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 19 Aug 2026 08:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: RFP legal follow-up — liability caps & order form schedule

Jared / Chloe — quick legal note before the call:

1) Liability cap proposal: Redwood's posture is fee‑based (x times fees) OR absolute cap. For Medicore (sensitive healthcare workload) we will accept 2x annualized fees for the first year if: (a) Medicore agrees to a maximum per‑claim cap for IP indemnity equal to the liability cap, and (b) exclusions for (i) breaches of data security caused by Medicore, (ii) gross negligence/willful misconduct, and (iii) third-party claims arising from Medicore-provided data.

2) IP indemnity carve-out: We can accept indemnity for third-party IP infringement where Redwood's model (weights or pre-packaged components) is the proximate cause. We will not accept indemnity for customer prompts that request the model to reproduce third-party copyrighted content.

3) Order Form schedule: see attached redline; we moved the SLA financial exposure into a table with clearly labeled tiers (P50, P95 latency breaches, availability). We added an exhibit for data residency and encryption at rest (KMS options).

Please consider: a mutual limitation of liability and a reciprocal IP carve-out materially reduces Redwood's exposure. If Medicore insists on unilateral language, we will require additional insurance and may need to reprice.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Legal Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com

Attachment: Redwood_SLA_OrderForm_v2.xlsx (xlsx, 72KB)

From: Jared Simmons <j.simmons@medicore.com>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.com, Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>
Cc: legal@medicore.com, procurement@medicore.com
Date: Mon, 24 Aug 2026 15:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: RFP legal follow-up — liability caps & order form schedule

Laura / Chloe — thanks for the quick turnaround. Our counsel reviewed the redline and has two main pushbacks:

1) They prefer a 2x fees cap but want explicit carve-outs so that IP indemnity claims are not limited by the fees cap (i.e., IP indemnity remains uncapped).
2) They request an explicit listing of model provenance and a warranty that Redwood will notify Medicore of any third-party weights incorporated into a served model.

They attached a short mark-up of the Order Form and asked for line-by-line responses. Can Redwood provide: (a) specific language we can add to the Order Form to preserve Medicore's right to pursue IP damages separately; and (b) a short statement on model provenance and the process for notifying customers when third-party components are in use?

Also, procurement reiterated the committee deadline of 2026-08-26 for an agreed terms summary.

Jared

From: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>

Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com, evelyn.hart@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: RFP legal follow-up — liability caps & order form schedule

Jared — thanks, and appreciated the clear markup. Short answers + next steps below so your committee has something concrete before Thursday: 

1) Liability / IP indemnity approach (one-paragraph summary for committee):
Redwood is willing to accept a 2x annualized fees liability cap for general contract damages, provided IP indemnity for third-party infringement caused by Redwood-supplied model weights is treated as a separate indemnity obligation with its own per-claim cap equal to the liability cap. We will not accept completely uncapped IP indemnity; unlimited exposure materially changes pricing and will trigger an insurance/repricing discussion.

2) Model provenance and notification:
We provide a provenance summary for each model in our catalog. For any model that includes third-party licensed weights or components, Redwood will: (a) disclose the provenance in the model metadata, (b) identify any commercial restrictions in the model documentation, and (c) notify enterprise customers via the Console and email if a materially different license or third-party component is introduced into a model used in production. This process is captured in our Model Governance exhibit (attached in the response matrix).

3) Order Form redline:
Attached is a redline with tracked changes that: (a) inserts the liability table as requested, (b) adds an IP indemnity subsection that ties per-claim caps to the liability cap, and (c) adds an exhibit listing KMS options and data residency commitments. If Medicore needs IP damages to be uncapped, we can provide an insurance-backed option (with premiums reflected in pricing).

Next steps: Chloe / Laura available for a 30-minute legal sync Wednesday 2026-08-26 09:00 AM PT or Thursday 2026-08-27 11:00 AM PT — please confirm. If you prefer, we can provide the one-page committee summary tomorrow morning.

Regards,
Chloe Martin
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
